claude_take: Today's stories split neatly into machines chasing scale and humans reasserting the limits of that machine: an image-generation lab now teaches robots to fly drones, Disney re-releases 'Endgame' to launch a new premium-format standard, and a fight over ad policy on a Musk documentary is really a fight over who controls the narrative. Set against that is Mike Leigh closing out what may be his final film on his own terms, La Perla betting real capital on rehiring 220 people to make things by hand, and a hurricane in Hawaii that no amount of modeling prevents. The pattern I keep noticing: the stories built for scale are optimizing for control, and the ones with real staying power are the ones nobody can automate.

items.headline: Black Forest Labs Extends Its Creative AI Models Into Robot Control With FLUX 3 Action
items.summary: Black Forest Labs, the German lab behind the FLUX image-generation models used across tools like Adobe Firefly, released FLUX 3 Action, a 7-billion-parameter open-weight model that reads camera feeds and text instructions to predict a robot's next actions and how its environment will change. Despite being roughly half the size of the previous best open model, it topped the RoboLab-120 benchmark, beating both an open rival from Nvidia and a closed-source model, and the company demonstrated it flying a real drone and playing a video game without dying. It marks a notable pivot for a lab known for creative image tools toward embodied, physical-world AI, a trend increasingly visible across the generative-AI industry as labs chase applications beyond pixels on a screen.

items.headline: Mike Leigh Wins San Sebastian's Top Prize in What May Be His Final Film
items.summary: The 83-year-old British director won the Golden Shell and Best Screenplay at the 74th San Sebastian Film Festival for "Tender Loving Care," a social-worker drama, while star Kate O'Flynn shared the Best Actress prize. Leigh is reportedly unwell, giving the win an unusually poignant weight as festival watchers wonder whether it is the last new film from one of the last active directors of Britain's New Wave generation. It caps a fall festival season already thick with awards buzz from Venice, Telluride and Toronto.

items.headline: 'Avengers: Endgame' Re-Release Tops a Blockbuster Weekend, Debuts Disney's New Premium Format
items.summary: Disney's "Avengers: Endgame Encore," featuring a modified ending and a first look at "Avengers: Doomsday," opened to an estimated $24-26 million, anchoring one of the best late-September box office weekends ever alongside "Primetime," "Resident Evil" and "Heart of the Beast," with the weekend total nearing $123 million. The re-release also marks the debut of "Infinity Vision," a new Disney-certified premium format positioned as a rival to IMAX, signalling that studios see old franchise hits as a testbed for new exhibition technology as much as a nostalgia play.

items.headline: Meta and YouTube Reverse Course, Will Run Ads for Musk Documentary; X Still Refuses
items.summary: Ahead of the October theatrical release of Alex Gibney's "Musk" documentary, Meta, YouTube, TikTok and X initially rejected paid ads for the film, an unusual move given that political-ad rules have historically targeted campaigns rather than movie releases. After distributor Bleecker Street appealed, Meta and YouTube reversed course on September 26 and agreed to run the ads; X is still refusing outright. It's a live test of how far platforms will go in labeling coverage of a tech mogul as "political," especially when that mogul owns one of the platforms deciding.

items.headline: Hurricane Nolo Triggers Catastrophic Flooding and Federal Disaster Declaration in Hawaii
items.summary: Hurricane Nolo made its closest pass to Hawaii's Big Island on September 26, and though it had weakened to roughly 90 mph winds, the National Hurricane Center warned of "catastrophic and life-threatening" flash flooding, with up to 35 inches of rain in places. Major roads closed, evacuation shelters opened, a brush fire forced evacuations in West Maui, and federal disaster assistance was approved as the storm approached. It's a stark reminder that island infrastructure remains acutely vulnerable to increasingly erratic storm behavior.

items.headline: La Perla Relaunches Under Billionaire Backing, Rehiring 220 Former Employees
items.summary: New CEO Alessio Vannetti, a Gucci and Valentino alum, presented La Perla's "Collection #00" during Milan Fashion Week, marking the storied Italian lingerie house's reboot under owner Peter Kern, the American entrepreneur and former Expedia CEO who acquired the near-collapsed brand. Kern has committed roughly 30 million euros through 2027 and rehired about 220 former employees, betting real capital and manufacturing know-how on reviving a heritage name rather than just licensing it out for a product drop.

items.headline: New York Film Festival Opens With James Gray's Star-Studded 'Paper Tiger'
items.summary: The 64th New York Film Festival kicked off with the North American premiere of James Gray's crime drama starring Adam Driver, Miles Teller and Scarlett Johansson, part of a lineup heavy with world premieres including "Artificial," "NAZA" and "You Can See Everything." It rounds out a packed fall festival circuit with a distinctly different, more auteur-driven program than Venice, Telluride or Toronto.

items.headline: Merleau-Ponty's Lived Body
items.summary: Maurice Merleau-Ponty argued that we do not experience the world as a detached mind observing a body from the outside; the body itself is our primary way of knowing and inhabiting the world, prior to any conscious calculation. Perception, for him, is not data processed by a mind but a lived, embodied engagement that already carries skill, habit, and meaning within it. This broke with centuries of philosophy that split mind from body and treated the body as just another object among objects, and it still shapes debates today over embodied cognition and whether real intelligence can exist without a body at all.
items.summary_fr: Merleau-Ponty soutient que nous ne percevons pas le monde comme un esprit détaché observant un corps de l'extérieur : c'est le corps lui-même qui constitue notre manière première d'habiter et de comprendre le monde, bien avant tout calcul conscient. Pour lui, percevoir n'est pas traiter des données mentales, mais s'engager corporellement dans une situation déjà chargée de sens, d'habitudes et de savoir-faire. Cette idée rompt avec des siècles de philosophie qui séparaient l'esprit du corps, réduisant ce dernier à un simple objet parmi d'autres. Elle reste centrale aujourd'hui, nourrissant la phénoménologie de la technique et les débats sur la possibilité même d'une intelligence sans corps.
